To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) consumers underestimate the cost of credit cards relative to market rates, (2) consumers can be taught to estimate the cost of credit card APR, and (3) the most effective method for communicating this information to consumers is a histogram of the market APR distribution.

(a) credit card disclosures containing only the average APR do not help consumers evaluate the costs of credit; (b) credit card disclosures that contain the full distribution of APRs can improve consumers’ estimates of credit card costs and help consumers to evaluate the relative cost of credit cards; (c) among different designs for displaying the distribution of APR costs, a histogram was most effective at helping consumers to evaluate credit cards; and (d) the effect of the histogram on consumers’ evaluations of credit cards

consumers’ estimates of the costs of credit cards are inaccurate when using standard credit card APR disclosures and that providing consumers with distributionally informative graphs improves their ability to estimate APR costs and evaluate credit card products.
